text: Soft ground, a patient creature, and a lot of worms. {lead} brings up the lot, and under them: Four-Leaf Clover.
{lead} tips the wheel over the lip and it bounds off downhill with great purpose. Where it was sitting: some loose change and a gratitude card.
The little round boat wobbles, then settles. {lead} crosses the water with short, careful strokes and lands among the reeds. There is Sea Glass.
Ripples run out from {lead}'s throw like a good rumour, and the stone raps a reed stem. Something drops out of it: Drake's Drum.
Ripples run out from {lead}'s throw like a good rumour, and the stone raps a reed stem. Something drops out of it: Aneroid Barometer.
{lead} peers into the water, then pulls out, with great ceremony, a purse, a bit damp.
A wall with a tooth missing. {lead} rebuilds it with no mortar and a great deal of dignity, and finds Rowan Sprig in the hollow.
A cheese wheel stuck in a hollow, as they do. {lead} gives it a shove and down the slope it goes, and the hollow gives up some loose change and a gratitude card.
{lead} peers into the water, then pulls out, with great ceremony, a roll of notes.
A dead trunk, leaning on nothing much. {lead} puts its shoulder to it and over it goes with a crack. Underneath: Hazelnuts.
Ripples run out from {lead}'s throw like a good rumour, and the stone raps a reed stem. Something drops out of it: Drake's Drum.
A coracle, left on the bank, light as a basket. {lead} gets in and paddles across without spinning more than twice. On the far side: Bakelite Radio.
A flat stone and a still stretch of water. {lead} sends it dancing across, once, twice, five times, and something on the far side wobbles loose: 1966 Final Ticket.
Sheep at the gate, and no sheep will go first. {lead} comes round the back, low and quiet, and the flock files through. The farmer's thanks: Flask of Tea.
A molehill, freshly heaped. {lead} drums a gentle rhythm on the ground and the worms come up to see what the fuss is. Among the soil: Field Mushrooms.
A wall with a tooth missing. {lead} rebuilds it with no mortar and a great deal of dignity, and finds some loose change and a gratitude card in the hollow.
A cheese wheel stuck in a hollow, as they do. {lead} gives it a shove and down the slope it goes, and the hollow gives up Somerset Cider.
The drystone has slumped. {lead} lifts the big stones in first and wedges the small ones after, which is exactly how it is done. Behind the stones: Rowan Sprig.
Bubbles rise in the peat. {lead} follows them down and brings up, to its evident pride, Ammonite.
